summary: Andrei Vostrikov (1904–1937) was a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky) and taught Bidia Dandaron.
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Harvard University (~1984–1990) and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (~1995).

Andrew Glass specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (MA 2000, PhD 2006 under Richard G. Salomon), also studying under Mark Allon, Ulrich Pagel, Sonam Wanggyal, and Gudrun Melzer.

Andrew Goudie is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Dean Close School (~1958–1963) and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1963–1969). He served as a professor at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.

Andrew J. Nicholson specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, having studied under traditional teacher Shrinarayan Mishra. He was appointed Associate Professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director of the Insight Meditation Society, Executive Director and Resident Scholar at Barre Center for Buddhist Studies, and senior scholar at Mind and Life Institute.

Andrew Ollett specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford (~2009–2011) and Columbia University (~2011–2017), later becoming an Associate Professor at the University of Chicago (~2023).

Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Andrew Quintman works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jay L. Garfield and has served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Sihler is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard College and Harvard University (~1958–1962), and at Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill (~1962–1967). He held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Madison (~1967–2000).

Andrew Watsky is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1988–1994), taught Bryan D. Lowe, and held a post at Vassar College (~1993–2008).
Andrew William Kennedy specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the doctoral supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Andrey Klebanov is an Indologist and linguist who earned his MA (2010) and PhD (2016) at the University of Hamburg, supervised by Harunaga Isaacson. He held posts at the University of Hamburg and Kyoto University (Professor, attested 2018–2021).

Andrey Terentyev is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University's Faculty of Philosophy (~1970–1975), worked at the Museum of the History of Religion (~1978–1992), and taught Ming Mei.

Andrzej Gawroński (1885–1927) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Lviv and University of Leipzig. He held posts at Jagiellonian University and the University of Lviv, and founded the Polish Oriental Society and Polish Linguistic Society.

András Róna-Tas is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, and held posts at the University of Szeged, University of Vienna, and International Association for Tibetan Studies.

André Bareau (1921–1993) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Sorbonne, Collège de France, and EPHE under Jean Filliozat and Paul Demiéville. He held posts at CNRS, EPHE, Collège de France, and Institut de civilisation indienne.

André Caquot (1923–2004) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand, École Normale Supérieure, and EPHE, later holding posts at EPHE, the University of Strasbourg, University of Paris, and Collège de France.

André Couture is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Laval University (~1964–1971), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1971–1977), and Paris-Sorbonne University (~1971–1977), and held a post at Laval University (~1979–2011).
